text: When I was twenty seven. <break time="0.8s" /> I was a clerk. <break time="0.8s" /> For a mining broker in San Francisco. <break time="0.8s" /> And I knew everything. <break time="0.8s" /> About the stock market. <break time="0.8s" /> I was alone in the world. <break time="0.8s" /> And I had nothing to depend on except my wits and my good name. <break time="0.8s" /> One Saturday afternoon. <break time="0.8s" /> I went sailing on the bay. <break time="0.8s" /> But a strong wind carried my little boat. <break time="0.8s" /> Far out to sea. <break time="0.8s" /> Just at nightfall. <break time="0.8s" /> A small ship bound for London. <break time="0.8s" /> Picked me up. <break time="0.8s" /> And I worked as a common sailor. <break time="0.8s" /> To pay for my passage. <break time="0.8s" /> When I stepped ashore in London. <break time="0.8s" /> My clothes were ragged. <break time="0.8s" /> And I had only one dollar. <break time="0.8s" /> In my pocket. <break time="0.8s" /> That dollar fed and sheltered me. <break time="0.8s" /> For twenty four hours. <break time="0.8s" /> But during the next day. <break time="0.8s" /> I had no food and no place to sleep. <break time="0.8s" /> The next morning. <break time="0.8s" /> As I dragged myself along Portland Place. <break time="0.8s" /> A child threw a big, juicy pear. <break time="0.8s" /> With only one bite gone. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the gutter. <break time="0.8s" /> I stopped and fixed my hungry eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> On that pear. <break time="0.8s" /> But every time I moved toward it. <break time="0.8s" /> Someone passing by looked at me. <break time="0.8s" /> I was just desperate enough. <break time="0.8s" /> To grab it. <break time="0.8s" /> When a window behind me opened. <break time="0.8s" /> And a gentleman called out. <break time="0.8s" /> Step in here, please. <break time="0.8s" /> If he had not called to me. <break time="0.8s" /> At that very moment. <break time="0.8s" /> I would have taken the pear. <break time="0.8s" /> In front of everyone.
